dedupe_keys.name: philippine general hospital spine building seismic fragility curves for a west valley fault earthquake

description: This case study assessed whether the spine building of the Philippine General Hospital in Manila, a tertiary hospital founded in 1907 and a COVID-19 facility, would survive a large West Valley Fault earthquake. The hospital sits about 9.2 kilometres from the fault. The authors, from Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila and USHER Technologies, built a SAP2000 model of the building, ran pushover analysis with the Capacity Spectrum Method under 12 worldwide and 12 local earthquake records from IRIS scaled from 0.1g to 3.0g, and derived fragility curves. They found the building might collapse at 0.538g peak ground acceleration, about Intensity VIII, compared with the 0.4g level required by the national structural code for Seismic Zone 4. The article is free to download as a PDF from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is one hospital building in Manila. Caveats: a single-building analytical study in a regional journal, with no model files or data tables released. Simulation uses: fragility parameters for hospital buildings in Metro Manila earthquake scenarios and a reference point for hospital functionality models. Related records: the Tuscany emergency department study (case_study-tuscany-emergency-department-seismic-resilience) looks at service loss, not structural collapse.
